title: Proportional Reasoning–2: Direct and Inverse Proportion

standard_text: Direct and inverse proportion, identifying proportional relationships and dividing in a given ratio (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 8)
meta_desc: Class 8 Proportional Reasoning–2 worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 3): direct proportion, inverse proportion, sharing in a ratio and ratio problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Direct: y ÷ x stays the same. Inverse: x × y stays the same
key_sub: More workers → fewer days: that is inverse proportion.
body_html:
How it works

In direct proportion, both quantities grow together and y ÷ x is constant (cost and number of items).

In inverse proportion, one grows as the other shrinks and x × y is constant (workers and days, speed and time).

To share in a ratio a : b : c, divide the total into a + b + c equal parts.

Example

6 workers take 10 days. How long do 4 workers take?

6 × 10 = 60 worker-days

60 ÷ 4

Answer: 15 days

Example

Share ₹900 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4.

9 parts: 1 part = ₹100

Answer: ₹200, ₹300, ₹400

Common mistakes

  • Treating an inverse situation as direct (more workers taking more days).
  • Adding the same amount instead of multiplying.
  • Dividing by one part instead of the total number of parts.

faq.a: Two quantities are in direct proportion when their ratio y ÷ x stays the same, so doubling one doubles the other.
Two quantities are in inverse proportion when their product x × y stays the same, so doubling one halves the other.

faq.q: How do you tell them apart?
faq.a: Ask: if one quantity doubles, does the other double (direct) or halve (inverse)?
